column1: # The switches that would switch what the gate's Rust tools check, named once. A line is:
#   Cargo configuration key <TAB> the environment variables Cargo reads that key from, space-separated
#   <TAB> what the committed rust/.cargo/config.toml may still set under the key, or - <TAB> why refused.
# The key holds `*` where any one name stands (a profile, a target, an alias, an [env] variable); the
# variables are the names Cargo derives from the key (uppercase, dots and dashes as underscores), plus the
# plain names the documentation lists beside the key (RUSTC for build.rustc, RUSTFLAGS for
# build.rustflags). A line with no key (the leading field -) is an environment-only switch, one with no
# variable (the second field -) a configuration-only one; a variable is capitals, digits and `_`, with one
# `*` at most, the one form a shell glob and the Rust reader match alike. A key two lines name is refused
# once, by the first. tools/env.sh reads this file to refuse the variables, and rust/xtask/src/upstream.rs
# reads it to refuse the same switches written as keys in any Cargo configuration Cargo reads for a build
# in rust/. The committed tree file may set the tree column of its key alone because that is what it holds
# today and nothing else was ever decided for it: today that is the alias xtask, and only while its value
# still runs the xtask package.
# Why a whole family and never a reading of the value, each settled by running it on the pinned toolchain
# against code the gate refuses. No reading of a flag list is safe: a flag reaches rustc after the lint
# table's (`--allow`, `--force-warn` and `--cap-lints` each silence a denied lint), `-C debug-assertions=on`
# hides the code under `cfg(not(debug_assertions))` from the release lint, an `@file` names more flags,
# and rustdoc hands the doctest harness its own (`--test-args=--skip=...` passes every doctest unrun). A
# compiler, a wrapper in front of it, rustdoc or rustfmt named here is handed every call and decides what
# reaches the pinned tool: a two-line wrapper appending `--cap-lints=allow` turns a clippy failure into a
# pass, and the gate cannot tell it from a cache, so sccache is refused with them. A runner stands in for
# every test binary (`true` passes them unrun), and a linker writes them (one that writes a passing script
# passes them too). Any other key of a target table overrides a dependency's build script
# ([target.<triple>.<links>]: an override that drops the cfg a dependency's build script sets turns a
# failing test into a pass). A profile variable or table overrides rust/Cargo.toml's profiles
# (debug-assertions on in release hides the same code). An [env] entry sets a variable for every process
# the build starts, over the gate's own when forced: a forced PATH hands rustc another `cc` to link with,
# and a forced CLIPPY_ARGS replaces the lint flags cargo clippy hands clippy. An alias stands in for a
# command the gate runs (`clippy = "test --no-run"` lints nothing). A build target sends the gate's own
# build of xtask to a <triple>/ folder inside the fresh build folder the run builds it in, where the gate,
# which runs its binary from that folder's debug/, cannot find it (tools/env.sh unsets CARGO_BUILD_TARGET,
# and tools/ci.sh runs only the xtask it built into that folder in that run). Another lockfile than
# rust/Cargo.lock passes --locked while the build takes its graph. RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP, and cargo's own
# __CARGO_TEST_CHANNEL_OVERRIDE_DO_NOT_USE_THIS, unlock the `-Z` flags and nightly configuration the
# pinned stable toolchain refuses (`cargo -Z unstable-options locate-project` exits 101 on the pin, 0 with
# either set); CARGO_UNSTABLE_* names a nightly feature; CLIPPY_CONF_DIR moves clippy to another
# clippy.toml.
# Left out, the rest of Cargo 1.99's configuration reference and of the variables it documents, each for
# its reason, run on the pinned toolchain where a run could tell:
#   paths, [patch] and [source] are the upstream rule's carriers (configuration_carriers and
#   environment_carriers in rust/xtask/src/upstream.rs), refused in every configuration and the
#   environment; include is followed, and what it brings in is read as the file that includes it.
#   build.target-dir and CARGO_TARGET_DIR: tools/env.sh sets the variable, which wins over every
#   configuration. build.build-dir moves the intermediates, and cargo still reports every artifact, with
#   its dep-info beside it, where the rules read them. build.dep-info-basedir rewrites the paths of that
#   dep-info into ones the rules resolve back to rust/ or fail to find, never a quieter reading.
#   build.warnings cannot lower a denied lint or the -D warnings every clippy stage passes (both still
#   fail beside warnings = "allow"). build.jobs, build.incremental and CARGO_INCREMENTAL, the unused
#   build.pipelining, CARGO_CACHE_RUSTC_INFO and resolver.incompatible-rust-versions (every gate
#   resolution is pinned by --locked) change what a build costs, never what a check reads.
#   [host] and [unstable] are read by a nightly cargo alone, or under the unlocks refused here: a host
#   runner, linker and rustflags leave a failing check failing either way, and a profile-rustflags bites
#   under no reading the gate can reach — the pinned stable cargo ignores the key, and honouring it takes
#   one of those refused unlocks, which the gate refuses before anything it runs can read the key.
#   http, net, registries, registry and credential-alias decide how and with whose credentials cargo
#   fetches, and a fetch delivers only the commits and checksums rust/Cargo.lock names; cache, term,
#   future-incompat-report, doc, cargo-new and install change what cargo cleans, prints or creates.
#   CARGO_HOME moves the cargo home, whose configuration the rules read wherever it is; CARGO is set by
#   cargo itself for everything it starts; CARGO_LOG, TERM, BROWSER, HTTPS_PROXY and HTTP_TIMEOUT change
#   what cargo prints or how it fetches. Outside Cargo: CLIPPY_ARGS in the environment, which cargo clippy
#   sets its own over (the [env] spelling of it is refused above), and CLIPPY_CONF_FILE, which clippy does
#   not read.
